digest.en: Norway and Finland leaders just finished frank talks with Putin while Israeli voters handed Netanyahu a record-turnout verdict. Meanwhile, Chinese markets shed trillions as the US AI race tightened its grip on global sentiment.
digest.hi: सऊदी अरब की तेल रिफाइनरी पर हूती मिसाइल हमले ने क्षेत्रीय तनाव को नई ऊंचाई पर पहुंचा दिया है। इसी बीच दक्षिण कोरिया की पूर्व फर्स्ट लेडी के खिलाफ सुप्रीम कोर्ट का कड़ा फैसला एशिया-प्रशांत में राजनीतिक अस्थिरता का संकेत देता है।

articles.title: Norway, Finland leaders hold 'frank and substantive' talk with Putin
articles.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store met with Vladimir Putin. They described the talks as frank and substantive. Stubb stated that ending the war requires direct discussions. The outcome will directly impact broader European security. "The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions," President Alexander Stubb said in a joint statement with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store.

articles.title: Record turnout as Israeli voters deliver verdict on Netanyahu
articles.summary: Israeli voters cast ballots in record numbers. The election took place amid the shadow of October 7 and ongoing regional wars. Campaigns focused heavily on security and accountability. The trauma of the attack remained a central theme for voters. Israelis are casting their ballots in the shadow of October 7 and the multi-front regional wars that it sparked, with the trauma from the attack still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign.

articles.title: ‘Will Lula’s win end Latin America’s far right turn?’: Our correspondent in Brazil answered your
articles.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential election in a second-round victory. He defeated far-right rival Flávio Bolsonaro. The result raised questions about the future of the region's political direction. Market reactions followed the announcement of the outcome. Having lost the first round of Brazil’s presidential election to far right rival Flávio Bolsonaro, incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva spectacularly triumphed in the second.

articles.title: Serbia Student List Lead Candidate Vows EU Integration, Open Debate On Russia Ties
articles.summary: Ilija Srdanovic leads Serbia's Student List party. The group recently ousted Aleksandar Vucic in elections. Srdanovic pledged to pursue EU integration. He also proposed a public debate on reconsidering sanctions against Russia. In an interview with RFE/RL, Ilija Srdanovic, the lead candidate for Serbia's Student List -- which ousted longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in recent elections -- pledged to pursue EU integration and said Belgrade's stance on sanctions against Russia could be reconsidered through public debate.

articles.title: 'Get Killed Or Starve': Life Under Russian Occupation In Oleshky
articles.summary: Residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky face severe food shortages and threats. Civilians risk mines and drone attacks to escape the area. A proposed cease-fire could open a humanitarian corridor. This would allow trapped civilians to leave the Ukrainian city. Residents fleeing Russian-occupied Oleshky describe hunger, soaring food prices, and threats from Russian soldiers. Cut off from supplies, civilians risk mines and drone attacks to escape.

articles.title: Lula’s win gives Brazil an opportunity to cement its climate leadership, but challenges remain
articles.summary: Lula begins his fourth term with the chance to strengthen Brazil's climate role. As Latin America's largest economy and Amazon steward, he can bridge divides among the EU, US, China, and BRICS. His diplomatic reach offers a path to more cohesive global climate agreements. In his fourth term, the President can potentially negotiate across the divides that currently frustrate climate agreements, given his country’s status as Latin America’s largest economy, host to most of the Amazon, and its diplomatic relationships with the EU, the U. S., China, the BRICS countries and other devel.

articles.title: Chasing foreign phantoms in Prabowo’s embattled Indonesia
articles.summary: Indonesian officials blame foreign actors for market crashes and peatland fires, deflecting from domestic accountability. Critics argue this narrative ignores local corporate ownership and political corruption. The strategy avoids addressing who actually controls listed companies and wins state contracts. Indonesia’s leaders promise that the country will be a world power by 2045, the centennial of its independence. Yet when shares plunge or smoke drifts abroad, officials reflexively blame foreigners.

articles.title: Record carbon dioxide levels will impact us for centuries, says UN weather agency
articles.summary: The World Meteorological Organization reported that carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases hit record highs in 2025. Burning fossil fuels drove these levels, locking in additional long-term global warming. The agency warned these atmospheric changes will affect the planet for centuries. Levels of carbon dioxide (CO2) and other major greenhouse gases in the atmosphere caused by burning fossil fuels reached record highs in 2025, locking in more long-term global warming, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll
articles.summary: Chinese stock markets lost trillions of dollars recently. Investors worry about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boom. The race for supremacy against the United States is straining profits and raising concerns about the sector’s future. Lack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boomTrillions of dollars have been wiped from China’s stock markets in recent months amid increasing anxiety about the future of artificial intelligence, as Beijing races against the United States for dominance in the sector. The STAR 50 Index, which tracks technology and innovatio.

articles.title: Cease-Fire in Ukraine's Oleshky Expanded To Help Flow Of Aid, Safe Passage
articles.summary: Russian air strikes hit Kyiv on October 26, targeting a university dormitory and other civilian buildings. At least one person died in the attacks. President Zelenskyy urged international partners to supply Ukraine with adequate defensive capabilities. Russian air attacks struck Kyiv late on October 26, hitting a university dormitory and other civilian sites, leaving at least one dead, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on Ukraine's partners to provide the "proper tools" for the country to defend itself.

articles.title: What Now For Serbia After Vucic's Stunning Election Defeat?
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic lost the Serbian parliamentary elections to student-led opposition. The ruling party was ousted from power. The new government must now navigate complex relations with the European Union, Russia, and China. Who will lead the next government of Serbia, after Aleksandar Vucic lost parliamentary elections, can the protest movement turn electoral success into stable rule, and what the result could mean for Serbia’s balancing relations with the European Union, Russia, and China?

articles.title: Iran, Regional Countries Agree To Continue Talks After Tehran Meeting
articles.summary: Mecca Defense Alliance partners met in Tehran to address regional conflicts. The snap meeting focused on stabilizing the Middle East. These tensions are currently disrupting global oil and cargo flows across the region. Officials from the so-called Mecca Defense Alliance have gathered for a snap meeting in Tehran as they look to settle conflicts in the Middle East that have left the region reeling and are impacting global flows of oil and other cargo.

articles.title: Women and girls’ share of civilian war deaths doubles since 2021
articles.summary: The United Nations reported that women and girls accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year. This figure represents a doubling of their share compared to 2021. The data highlights a significant shift in the demographic impact of global wars. Civilian casualties have risen sharply during this period. War is growing deadlier for women and girls, who accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year – double their share in 2021 – according to major UN report released Monday.

articles.title: Investigators find Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians
articles.summary: A panel of human rights experts concluded that Russian forces committed war crimes and crimes against humanity during the Ukraine invasion. The findings cite deliberate attacks on civilians and vital energy infrastructure. These actions violate international law. The report details specific violations of protected targets. Top human rights experts investigating Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine said on Monday that the Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity by attacking civilians and vital energy infrastructure, among other violations of international law.

articles.title: US forces accused of ‘weaponising’ Somalia’s floods by trapping women and children in the path of
articles.summary: US airstrikes in southern Somalia are pushing civilians toward the rising River Juba. Women and children face drowning risks as they flee al-Shabaab territory. Humanitarian groups accuse the military of weaponizing the flood crisis. The strategy traps vulnerable populations in dangerous waterways. Exclusive: Coordinated airstrikes on territory held by al-Shabaab are driving the civilian population to find refuge alongside a river where rising water levels are a threat to safety.

articles.title: Bizarre hobby takes seed among China’s stressed young adults
articles.summary: Young Chinese adults are raising bricks instead of children or pets due to a stagnant job market. Bricks are low-maintenance and cost almost nothing. This hobby offers a cheap alternative to traditional responsibilities, allowing stressed workers to avoid the financial burden of dating or raising offspring. Faced with a stagnant jobs market, many are spurning children or pets in favour of ‘raising bricks’Young adults in China looking for a cheaper, low-maintenance alternative to having children or pets have found an answer: raising bricks. Bricks may not be as cuddly as cats or as life-affirming as human offspring, but they also cost next to nothing.

articles.title: Why Lula’s ‘miracle’ win matters well beyond Brazil
articles.summary: Lula secured a surprising victory over Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil. The win reversed a significant first-round deficit. It signals a major shift in global politics. The outcome impacts climate policy and international relations beyond South America. Three weeks ago, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s political obituaries had all been written. The far-right presidential candidate, Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro, had come out of the first round of the presidential election with a lead that looked impossible to overcome.

articles.title: Does Japan need nuclear subs? The debate is bigger than China
articles.summary: Japan is debating the acquisition of nuclear-powered submarines. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi opened the discussion in parliament. The decision is part of a 2026 security review. The debate extends beyond countering China to broader strategic autonomy. Japan’s debate over nuclear-powered submarines is gaining momentum, but political deliberation should not be mistaken for a done deal. As Tokyo prepares to revise its three principal national security documents by the end of 2026, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has opened the door to a long-politically sensitive capability.

articles.title: Student-Led Opposition Celebrates In Serbia After Vucic Concedes Election Defeat
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia's October 25 parliamentary elections. The student-led Students' List took a decisive lead in preliminary results. This ends his fourteen-year dominance of Serbian politics. Former President Aleksandar Vucic, who dominated Serbian politics for the past 14 years, conceded defeat in the country's parliamentary elections after polls closed on October 25. Preliminary results showed the movement called Students' List taking a decisive lead.

articles.title: Vucic Concedes Electoral Defeat, Setting Stage For New Era Of Serbian Politics, Relations With West
articles.summary: Vucic admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in Serbia's parliamentary vote. His concession signals a potential shift toward European alignment. The new government may distance Serbia from Kremlin influence. Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's former president and dominant political figure for more than a decade, conceded defeat to the student-led protest movement in the country's parliamentary elections, potentially ushering in a new era of politics more closely aligned with Europe and away from the Kremlin.

articles.title: Why do planes keep circling before landing? UN has a plan to fix it
articles.summary: The UN aviation agency is pushing for better air traffic coordination to reduce circling flights. Current delays cost billions and increase emissions. Some countries have already proven that improved coordination saves thousands of flying hours. The agency wants the rest of the world to adopt these proven methods. Air traffic delays cost billions and turn journeys into ordeals. Some countries are already proving that better coordination saves thousands of flying hours and cuts emissions – and the UN’s aviation agency wants the rest of the world to follow.

articles.title: Relentless Russian Strikes Drive Civilians From Ukraine's Kramatorsk
articles.summary: Ukraine ordered mandatory evacuations for families with children in Kramatorsk and Slovyansk. Russian forces intensified strikes across the Donetsk region. The move aims to protect civilians as Moscow pushes to seize the entire area. As Russian forces intensify attacks on Ukraine’s Donetsk region, evacuations are accelerating in Kramatorsk, a key city still held by Kyiv. As Moscow seeks to seize all of the Donetsk region, Ukraine has issued a mandatory evacuation order for families with children in Kramatorsk and Slovyansk.

articles.title: Women ‘first to suffer’ under siege, first to step up as frontline responders in Sudan
articles.summary: Tahani Al-Numeiri in Khartoum mistook the initial explosions for wedding celebrations on 15 April 2023. The Rapid Support Forces had just opened fire on the army. Women in Sudan now serve as frontline responders during the siege. They face immediate danger while managing critical aid distribution. The conflict has forced them into roles previously held by men. Their work sustains communities under active bombardment.

articles.title: Will Trump Help Putin Win in Ukraine?
articles.summary: Crisis Group experts discussed the rift between Washington and Kyiv. They analyzed Russia’s intensifying attacks on Ukraine. European capitals are working to strengthen Ukraine while facing their own political and economic pressures. This week on Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group experts Lucian Kim, Stephen Pomper and Fabienne Hara about the latest rift between Washington and Kyiv, Russia’s intensifying attacks and European capitals’ efforts to strengthen Ukraine while themselves under pressure.

articles.title: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.summary: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in over a decade. The patient is the wife of a Swiss diplomat who traveled in Uganda. Health officials are racing to determine the infection source as fears grow about further spread. Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in UgandaHealth officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country. articles.summary: उत्तर और दक्षिण कोरिया की सीमा पर तीन बख्तरबंद तोपें दिखाई दीं। इनमें एक 122 मिमी हॉवित्जर शामिल है जिसकी मारक दूरी 15 मील है। दक्षिण कोरियाई विशेषज्ञों ने इसे ताकत दिखाने की कोशिश बताया। North Korea News: उत्तर कोरिया और दक्षिण कोरिया के बीच तनाव के बीच सीमा के पास तीन बख्तरबंद तोपें दिखाई दी हैं. इनमें एक 122 मिमी की सेल्फ-प्रोपेल्ड हॉवित्जर तोप मानी जा रही है, जिसकी मारक दूरी करीब 15 मील है.

articles.title: डीआर कांगो में नहीं थम रहा इबोला, 10,000 पार हुए मामले
articles.summary: डीआर कांगो में इबोला प्रकोप जारी है। देश में मामलों की संख्या 10,000 से पार हो गई है। प्रयासों के बावजूद संक्रमण कम नहीं हो रहा है। स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली पर दबाव बना हुआ है। देश में इबोला कहर बरपा रहा है और काफी कोशिशों के बावजूद भी इसके मामले कम होने का नाम नहीं ले रहे हैं। अब डीआर कांगो में इबोला के मामलों पर एक बड़ा अपडेट सामने आया है।

articles.title: कीव पर रूसी मिसाइल हमले से मचा हड़कंप, 12 घायल; जेलेंस्की बोले- रूस पर दबाव जरूरी
articles.summary: रूसी सेना ने कीव पर 16 बैलिस्टिक मिसाइलों से हमला किया, जिसमें एक विश्वविद्यालय परिसर पर हमले से 12 लोग घायल हुए। जेलेंस्की ने यूरोप और अमेरिका से रूस पर दबाव बनाने की अपील की। Russia Ukraine War: यूक्रेन के राष्ट्रपति वोलोदिमीर जेलेंस्की ने बताया कि, एक यूनिवर्सिटी कैंपस पर रूसी हमले में 12 लोग घायल हो गए हैं। जेलेंस्की ने दावा किया कि रूस ने रात भर चले अपने हमले में कुल 16 बैलिस्टिक मिसाइलें दागीं।
